latest_findings.claim: With m2 fixed at 0.5, the N=64 to N=128 drop in trained force R2 does not go away. At N=128 (best layer 4), trained force R2 is 0.693 (seed 20) and 0.684 (seed 21), against 0.763 and 0.789 for the same seeds in the paired N=64 m2-fixed arm. That is a drop of 0.070 and 0.105, close to the wide-m2 drop of 0.08-0.13. The force controls barely move (seed 20: about 0.63 to 0.630; seed 21: about 0.594 to 0.583, change of 0.012 or less), so the whole drop is in trained R2. The force margin falls from 0.133/0.195 to 0.063/0.101, and seed 20 no longer beats its control. In contrast, accel_step stays strong: R2 0.945/0.933 vs control 0.793/0.760, margin 0.152/0.173, headroom-normalised margin 0.74/0.72. Layer-1 distance R2 falls only a little (0.950/0.926 to 0.915/0.908). The force loss at N=128 is therefore in reading out 1/r^2, not in the m2 factor.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds completed all 3000 steps and both show a drop of at least 0.06 with flat controls, which matches the expected-if-false outcome. The N=64 baseline values (0.763/0.789) come from the paired arm's earlier finding, not from probes_final of this experiment. The paired-arm trajectory gives 0.768 for seed 20, which may be the max-over-layers field. N=64 controls were inferred as R2 minus margin. Seed 20's drop (0.070) is only 0.01 above the 0.06 bar, so a probes_final N=64 value below 0.753 would make that seed inconclusive. The best layers also differ for seed 21: force peaks at layer 1 (the distance layer) at N=64 and at layer 4 at N=128, so part of the drop may be a layer-1 force signal that disappears. The comparison is at matched training step, not matched loss (N=128 val_mse_ratio is 0.048-0.056). The verdict would change if the drop shrinks below 0.03 when both arms are read at matched val_mse_ratio, or if more seeds (22-23) show drops under 0.06.

latest_findings.claim: With m2 fixed at 0.5, the N=256 force random-control R2 is 0.6197 (seed 20, layer 1) and 0.6521 (seed 21, layer 3). The paired N=128 m2-fixed arm has no probes_final yet, so the planned comparison was not computed. Its trajectory gives controls of at most about 0.633 (seed 20) and 0.583 (seed 21), which suggests the seeds disagree: about -0.013 or more for seed 20 and about +0.069 or more for seed 21. Separately, trained force fails to beat control at N=256 in both seeds (R2 0.648 vs control 0.620, margin 0.028; R2 0.655 vs control 0.652, margin 0.003), while accel_step clears the bar easily (R2 0.935 vs control 0.770, margin 0.165, normalised 0.72; R2 0.930 vs control 0.716, margin 0.213, normalised 0.75). Force margin falls with N in both seeds even with m2 fixed (N=64 0.133/0.195, N=128 0.063/0.101, N=256 0.028/0.003, from trajectories).
latest_findings.confidence_note: The hypothesis said to read the N=128 control from probes_final and to report the comparison as not computed if that was unavailable. It is unavailable because exp-20261013-231210-ae2c is still analyzing. The N=128 controls above were worked out as trajectory R2 minus margin. That trajectory R2 is a max over layers, not the R2 at the best-margin layer: for this experiment's own runs it reads 0.657/0.665 against probes_final 0.648/0.655. So the derived N=128 controls are upper bounds that may be about 0.01 too high, and the per-seed rises are lower bounds. Seed 21 clears the +0.03 bar even under that bias. Seed 20 could fall anywhere from below the N=128 value up into the 0.01-0.03 inconclusive band. The best-margin layer also differs between arms (N=256 layers 1/3 vs N=128 layer 4), so the controls are not compared at the same layer. Control spread is 0.022-0.030, close to the size of the effect being tested. Only 2 seeds and 1 data_seed. Both runs completed 3000/3000 steps and beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.196/0.243). The accel_step part of the true-prediction is met in both seeds (margin >= 0.1, normalised 0.72/0.75 inside [0.55, 0.85]). What would change the verdict: once the N=128 m2-fixed probes_final exist, a supported verdict needs seed 20's control to be <= 0.590, and a refuted verdict needs seed 21's to be >= 0.642. The trajectory bound already makes the second unlikely.

latest_findings.claim: With m2 fixed at 0.5 (N=64, e<=0.5, 3000 steps), force is still decoded above its best-of-3 control in both seeds: seed 21 has R2 0.789 vs control 0.594 (margin 0.195, layer 1) and seed 20 has R2 0.763 vs control 0.630 (margin 0.133, layer 4). accel_step does better in both seeds, with R2 0.940/0.957 vs control 0.771/0.799 at layer 4, a headroom-normalised margin of 0.74/0.79 against force's 0.48/0.36. Trained force R2 is higher than in the wide-m2 runs of the same seeds (0.726/0.737), but the margins are smaller (wide-m2 0.215/0.261) because fixing m2 raises the force control from about 0.48-0.51 to 0.59-0.63.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds meet every expected-if-true criterion: force margin >= 0.12, trained force R2 in [0.62, 0.85], and normalised accel_step margin in [0.55, 0.85]. Both runs completed 3000/3000 steps and beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.011-0.012). Values are read from probes_final, unrounded. Seed 20's force margin (0.133) is only 0.013 above the 0.12 bar and peaks at layer 4, not at the distance layer as in seed 21, so the best force layer is not stable across seeds. There are only two seeds and one data_seed (0). The comparison with wide-m2 runs mixes a change in the trained R2 with a change in the control, so the smaller margin here does not mean m2 adds decodable structure. Fixing m2 removes the m2 part of the force target, which makes it easier for random models to read. The verdict would change if a third seed or data_seed 1 gave a force margin below 0.10. In both seeds the force margin was still rising at step 3000 (+0.006 to +0.011 per 500 steps), so 3000 steps is not a plateau.

latest_findings.claim: On data_seed 1, both fresh N=256 seeds lose their force margin to rising random controls. Force control R2 is 0.6531 (seed 23) and 0.5839 (seed 22), against N=128 controls of at most about 0.55 and 0.52 (rises of >= ~0.10 and >= ~0.06). The final force margins are 0.096 and 0.069, so neither beats its control, while accel_step clears its control easily (R2 0.926/0.917 vs control 0.715/0.756; headroom-normalised 0.74/0.66). Trained force R2 does not stay flat as predicted: it rises in seed 23 (0.7486 at N=256 vs at most ~0.714 at N=128, about +0.035) and falls in seed 22 (0.6532 vs at most ~0.696, a drop of up to about 0.043). So the control-rise half of the hypothesis holds in both seeds, but the |delta trained R2| <= 0.02 condition fails in both, in opposite directions.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both runs completed 3000/3000 steps and beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.337-0.346). The paired N=128 values were not computed as pre-registered: the N=128 arm's probes_final was not available to me, so N=128 trained R2 comes from the trajectory's 4th field and control R2 from that field minus margin. In these N=256 runs that field overstates the probes_final best-layer R2 by 0.004-0.017 (0.753 vs 0.7486; 0.670 vs 0.6532). The N=128 values are therefore upper bounds. As a result, seed 22's trained drop lies somewhere in about 0.026-0.043, which straddles the 0.04 refutation bar. Seed 23's trained rise could be larger than +0.035. Every control rise is a lower bound. Seed 23's force control_spread is 0.049, so control noise is a large part of the effect. Reading N=128 probes_final directly would settle seed 22 against the 0.04 bar. A drop >= 0.04 there would make this refuted. A drop <= 0.02 in both seeds would make it supported. With two seeds whose trained-R2 changes have opposite signs, the trained-vs-control decomposition of the N=128-to-N=256 step looks noisy at the +/-0.04 level. The one robust result is the control rise.

latest_findings.claim: Fresh seeds 22-23 at N=64 on data_seed 1 have higher force than the seeds 20-21 reference: both final force margins (0.275 and 0.268) and both trained R2 values (0.809 and 0.793) are above the predicted ranges ([0.18, 0.26] and [0.68, 0.78]), while force controls (0.534 and 0.525) match the reference. accel_step stays the stronger readout: R2 0.926-0.937 at layer 4 against controls of 0.761-0.774, a raw margin of only 0.163-0.165 but a headroom-normalised margin of 0.69-0.72, versus 0.59-0.58 normalised for force. val_mse_ratio is 0.017-0.019.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Neither the expected-if-true nor the expected-if-false outcome occurred. Force is above control in both seeds, well clear of the 0.15 / 0.65 failure bars, but both seeds overshoot the upper bounds for margin and trained R2. The two fresh seeds agree with each other to within 0.007 in margin and 0.016 in trained R2. They sit about 0.06 above seeds 20-21 (0.209). The controls are the same, so the gap is entirely in trained R2 (0.79-0.81 vs about 0.74). The data_seed 1 N=64 force level therefore does depend on the model seed, by about 0.06, which the hypothesis did not anticipate. seeds_agree is false because the verdict is inconclusive, not because the seeds disagree. Force was still rising at step 3000 (+0.010 per 500 steps in seed 23, +0.007 in seed 22), so the final value also depends on training length. Paired context, computed from the sibling arm's trajectories (4th field, which may be max over layers rather than the best-margin layer; force best layer is 1 at every checkpoint in all four runs) and not cited as evidence: the per-seed N=64-to-N=128 trained force R2 drop is 0.095 (seed 23) and 0.097 (seed 22). The margin drop is 0.112 and 0.095. Implied N=128 controls are 0.55 and 0.52, so this step is almost entirely in trained R2, as in seeds 20-21. A matched-loss reading uses the N=64 step-1500 checkpoint (val_mse_ratio 0.073 and 0.081, close to N=128's step-3000 values). There, N=64 trained force R2 is 0.761 and 0.750 against N=128's 0.714 and 0.696, a gap of 0.047-0.054, so the N=64-to-N=128 shortfall is not explained by convergence alone. This reading uses the trajectory field and should be rechecked from per-layer probes. Two or more further seeds at about 0.21 would make seeds 22-23 look like the outliers. Two or more at about 0.27 would make seeds 20-21 the outliers.
